resources.string: Insulin timings are fit ONLY within a ±20% corridor around the measured profile — read from the per-segment analysis of your own injections — and cannot be swapped for a number that merely fits the chart better. Carb queue and type ratios move within physiological bounds. ISF is free: it really does drift, and catching that drift is part of the app\'s job.

The numbers are loaded into the fields above, but NOT applied. The spread in parentheses is disagreement between episodes, not error: when it\'s wide, the median doesn\'t describe every day equally.

WHAT WAS MEASURED: the ramp (“trust”) holds back half the food and insulin at the hour mark, and because of it a late peak buys extra insulin effect for free — that is, timing leaks into amount. With the ramp off, fitting its 22 episodes gives a 40–42 min peak in 13 cases.

WHAT WAS NOT MEASURED: what happens to hypo alerts. The direction is earlier, i.e. toward safety, but how much earlier is not checked. Model review hasn\'t happened yet. And fitting by “balance” pulls ISF down, eating into a food shortfall: look at the “shape” arm if you want sensitivity specifically.
